when: The speaker defines parts of a concept
why: Each new part has a stable location and explicit meaning
avoid: Do not force a full vocabulary list into one short

when: The same question changes meaning with a definition
why: Preserving the question makes the change in meaning visible
avoid: Do not invent a correct answer or measured improvement

why: Direction and labels separate ownership from consumption
avoid: Do not imply the ontology owns source DAX

when: A rule or schema is confused with running automation
why: The gap prevents implying automatic execution
avoid: Do not show successful notification without actual evidence

when: Different engines or refresh paths matter
why: Parallel lanes keep route differences legible
avoid: Do not promise live data for every path

when: The speaker explains how to verify an answer
why: The viewer can follow the verification path
avoid: Do not use a citation badge as proof of correctness

when: The actor or execution credentials matter
why: Labels explain the boundary; a shield alone does not
avoid: Do not merge interactive-user and operations-creator identity
